data.text:
AFP Chief Supports PBBM’s Vision for Defense Modernization, Participates in Post-SONA Policy Talks

The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP), under the leadership of General Romeo S Brawner Jr., successfully carried out its mission to ensure a safe, orderly, and peaceful environment during the 4th State of the Nation Address (SONA) of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. held at the Batasan Complex, Quezon City, on July 28.

In close coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), and the Legislative Security Bureau (LSB) of the House of Representatives, the AFP deployed around 2,500 personnel to perform vital roles in area security, crowd control, emergency response, and quick reaction operations.

On July 30, General Brawner joined key government officials during the Post-SONA Discussions at the Makabagong San Juan National Government Center in San Juan City. The event served as a venue to further unpack and align sectoral and agency-level efforts with the priorities laid out in the President’s address—particularly on national security, defense modernization, and whole-of-nation development.

General Brawner reaffirmed the AFP’s support for the Revised AFP Modernization Program, which is at the core of the defense sector’s transformation and capability development. He emphasized the importance of the Comprehensive Archipelagic Defense Concept (CADC) in enhancing maritime security and ensuring a credible defense posture.

The AFP also welcomed the President’s recognition of its counterinsurgency gains—highlighting the dismantling of guerrilla fronts, the reintegration of former rebels, and sustained peacebuilding initiatives in areas such as the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

With strengthened interagency collaboration and continued community engagement, the AFP reaffirms its mission to protect the people, defend the territory, and help shape a peaceful and prosperous nation.

Photos by PFC Carmelotes PN(M) / PAOAFP

data.text:
Traffic Advisory 

01 August 2025

ROADS AFFECTED BY THE MTN 8 MATCH BETWEEN ORLANDO PIRATES FC AND POLOKWANE CITY FC IN ORLANDO, SOWETO

Motorists are advised of traffic disruptions around Orlando Stadium for the MTN 8 Quarter-final match between Orlando Pirates FC and Polokwane City FC in Orlando, Soweto, Saturday, 02 August 2025.

Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD) officers will be deployed to ensure the free flow of traffic around Orlando Stadium and to ensure the safety of all road users. 

The following routes will be affected:

N17, Soweto Highway, Klipspruit Valley Road, Martha Louw Street, and Mooki Street.

Road closures will be implemented at 11h00.

Road closures will be implemented on: 

Mooki Street between Nkom Ya Hlaba and Masopha Streets. Also, expect closures on Martha Louw Street between Klipspruit Valley Road and Mooki Street, and at Adams and Rathebe Streets next to the YMCA and Adams and Nzama Streets

The following alternative routes can be used in the affected areas: 

From Mooki Street, motorists can use Ballenden and Masupa Street. Motorists can also use Soweto Highway and Klipspruit Valley Road.

Parking for spectators will be at an open space by the corner of Martha Louw Street and Klipspruit Valley Road, Shomane High School, AB Quma Primary School (Scott Street), Lofentse Girls High School (Mooki Street), Zithathele Primary School (Mooki Street), Leratong Primary School, Orlando High School, Selelekela High School (Mooki Street), Lereche Primary School Adams Street), Orlando Rugby Field (Adams Street), and Orlando Court (Mooki Street). VIP’s, Media, and VOC members' parking will be inside Orlando Stadium.

Residents and members of the public are urged to exercise patience for the duration of the match as we expect traffic disruptions in the area.

Gates will open at 12h00, and the kick-off will be at 15h00, so it is appealing for spectators to arrive early to avoid congestion before the match.

We are further appealing to road users to acquaint themselves with the traffic management for the day so they can plan their routes accordingly.

Ends.

Issued by the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department's Communications Unit #JoburgRoadSafety #JHBTraffic #NomakanjaniManjeNamhlanje #SaferJoburg #MTN8
